question: Should OpenClaw treat a reachable same-package, same-signature paired Wear OS watch as an operator-authorized client for session/history access, prompt sending, and run aborts, and ship that surface through the official Android release process now?
rationale: The transport is platform-authenticated and credential-free, but accepting a paired watch as an operator delegate and committing to a new official application and release track are product and security choices that tests cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve the phone-proxy boundary
options.body: Sponsor the official Wear companion with the current allowlist after exact-head physical proof and Google Play release-path validation.

options.title: Ship a status-only first phase
options.body: Narrow the initial release to connectivity status while separately reviewing conversation access, prompt sending, abort, notifications, voice, and TTS.

options.title: Pause official Wear support
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open but do not merge a first-party Wear application until ownership and long-term release support are confirmed.

recommendation.title: Approve the phone-proxy boundary
recommendation.body: Sponsor the official Wear companion with the current allowlist after exact-head physical proof and Google Play release-path validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository documentation identifies this person as the Android app owner, so they are best positioned to accept the application, trust, and release obligations.
